sources.title: Central African dwarf crocodiles found in syntopy are comparably divergent to South American dwarf caimans
sources.locator: Abstract; sampling; genomic results; discussion of hybridization.
sources.scope: Survey and genomic comparison of a small dwarf-crocodile sample from a syntopic site in northwestern Republic of the Congo; supports the local co-occurrence record and divergence comparison in the study sample, while the authors call for larger samples.
sources.attribution: Gvoždík L et al. (2024). Central African dwarf crocodiles found in syntopy are comparably divergent to South American dwarf caimans. Biology Letters 20(5):20230448. DOI 10.1098/rsbl.2023.0448. Claims are paraphrased.

claims.text: The survey found Osteolaemus osborni and O. tetraspis at one forest-swamp site in northwestern Republic of the Congo; genomic comparisons used more than 400 nuclear loci and the authors requested larger samples to assess hybridization.
claims.scope: One site and a small genomic sample; not an estimate of range-wide co-occurrence, gene flow, or hybridization frequency.

gaps: No multi-source species dossier is added.
The limited syntopic sample cannot support a range-wide frequency or gene-flow estimate.
